title: Move ELK to standalone package
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Splits Flowchart-ELK into a separate package, to make licensing simpler.

Resolves #5043 

This allows sites to fallback to dagre layout for `flowchart-elk` if the elk package is not installed, instead of completely breaking rendering.
We need to pick either #5050 or #5051 for the approach to override.

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

Moved files to a new package, removed elkjs dependency from the mermaid core.
Edited tsconfig to allow import of files from mermaid, to avoid duplicating code. 

### :clipboard: Tasks

Make sure you

- [x] :book: have read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] :computer: have added necessary unit/e2e tests.
author: sidharthv96

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: It doesn't have to be in this PR, but at some point, we really need to optimise this.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body: Since we're now using `prettier` instead of `standard`, I think we should be able to remove this.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
I think we should make this a `peerDependency` and using [`pnpm`'s `workspace:^` protocol](https://pnpm.io/workspaces#workspace-protocol-workspace).

That way, whenever we do an `pnpm publish`, it should automatically use the latest version of Mermaid. And it also means that if we ever made a breaking change to Mermaid, we won't break any existing plugins.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
What about:

```suggestion
    "build:types": "pnpm --recursive exec tsc --emitDeclarationOnly",
```

Very simple, and it runs in parallel (by default it's 4 jobs, see https://pnpm.io/cli/recursive#--workspace-concurrency).

The only potential issue is that 4 jobs might use up a lot of RAM (does tsc use up a lot of RAM?), but we could lower this with `--workspace-concurrency=2` or something.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
It should not run in parallel.

Parser first, mermaid second, then the other packages. 

Otherwise it won't compile.
